newsitem.title: SWITZERLAND: Swiss shares lose steam but still end higher.
newsitem.headline: Swiss shares lose steam but still end higher.

text.p: 1430 GMT - Swiss shares lost steam towards the end of the session as profit taking set in after the blue-chip Swiss Market Index (SMI) failed to overcome a resistance level around 3,765/70 points.

Volumes were high, bolstered by derivatives-linked transactions, one dealer said. He added sentiment remained good but warned it may turn negative in the next few days. "We will probably see further advances until the Dow Jones reaches 6,000 points. After that, we might be in for a major correction".
* The SMI gained 0.61 percent, or 22.7 points, to 3,760.2.
* Broad SPI up 0.52 percent, or 12.38 points, to 2,407.14.
* Heavily-traded Roche certificates were buoyed by a buy recommendation and foreign demand, dealers said. The stock jumped 125 francs to 9,375.
* Ciba and Sandoz were hit by profit taking towards the session's close. Ciba registered shares ended flat at 1,610. Sandoz fell three francs to 1,512.
* Among financials, insurers, CS Holding and UBS bearer shares posted marked gains.
A dealer said news that two of CS Holding's banking units would close 21 small retail branches and counters in Switzerland by the end of 1996 did not affect the stock much.
* ABB and Alusuisse added eight and six francs, respectively.
* Sulzer profited from derivatives-linked buys and technical factors. The shares were up four francs to 745.
* Among second-tier serurities, technology group Esec stood out with a gain of 2.5 percent.
